sections.overview: The Coscoroba is a small, distinctive South American swan-like waterfowl placed in its own genus, Coscoroba.
sections.identification: Adults are white with black primary tips and a red bill, and are smaller and shorter-necked than the larger swans.
sections.habitat: It uses shallow freshwater lagoons, marshes and lakes with abundant vegetation, and can also occupy some coastal wetlands.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on aquatic plants and small invertebrates by dabbling or wading, and also grazes on nearby pasture.
sections.behavior: It often feeds in shallow water without upending as frequently as other swans, and may gather in pairs or small groups outside breeding.
sections.reproduction: Breeding is concentrated in the southern part of its South American range, while seasonal movements farther north remain incompletely known.
sections.ecology: Its broad bill has fine serrations that help strain food particles, and it overlaps geographically with the black-necked swan without belonging to the genus Cygnus.
sections.conservation: The global status cited is Least Concern, although the patchy distribution makes local wetland loss and local disappearance relevant concerns.
